slots.bio: A Flemish Renaissance gem of basalt and limestone, with a mosaic-floored hall — New Zealand's most photographed building.
A Gothic Revival mansion high on the Otago Peninsula, with lavish interiors and celebrated gardens.
At Taiaroa Head, a hide overlooks the world's only mainland breeding colony of northern royal albatross.
A conservation reserve where trenches and hides bring you close to endangered yellow-eyed penguins.

slots.bio: Natural history, Pacific and Māori cultures, a tropical butterfly house and a planetarium beside the university.
The story of Otago told through Māori, Scottish and Chinese settlers, vintage trams and a hall of portraits.
A short residential street so steep it has held the title of the world's steepest — walk up if you dare.
Sandstone sea arches and a hand-carved Victorian tunnel leading down to a hidden cove.
Giant sand dunes tumble down to a wild beach where New Zealand sea lions often doze on the sand.
